full_text_en:
Jingxiutang (Pharmaceutical) Co., Ltd. v. Huanghua Printing House — dispute over telephone charges

Plaintiff: Guangzhou Jingxiutang (Pharmaceutical) Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Xiao Cheng, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Lin Miaohong, Head of the Security Section of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Wugui, Lawyer of Guangzhou Yuexiu Law Firm.

Defendant: Guangzhou Dongshan District Huanghua Printing House.

Legal Representative: Su Guoxiong, Director of the Printing House.

Agent ad litem: Xu Yaomin, Lawyer of Guangzhou Dongshan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lu Weiguo, Judicial Officer of Dongshan District Huanghua Street Legal Affairs Office.

The plaintiff, Guangzhou Jingxiutang (Pharmaceutical) Co., Ltd., filed a lawsuit with the Dongshan District People's Court of Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, regarding a dispute over compensation for telephone charges arising from the defendant, Guangzhou Dongshan District Huanghua Printing House, allegedly using the plaintiff's telephone password to make international long-distance calls without authorization.

The Dongshan District People's Court found the following facts after trial: The plaintiff, Guangzhou Jingxiutang (Pharmaceutical) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jingxiutang Company), began using a password-protected telephone in 1985. Between September and November 1990, the plaintiff's telephone charges increased sharply, prompting the plaintiff to report the matter to the public security authorities. Upon investigation, the detailed computer records of international manual telephone calls from the telecommunications bureau showed that during this period, someone used the plaintiff's telephone password, employing the telephone set of the defendant, Guangzhou Dongshan District Huanghua Printing House (hereinafter referred to as Huanghua Printing House), to make 22 international long-distance calls, including 7 during the day and 15 at night, resulting in a loss of RMB 3,650.10 in telephone charges for the plaintiff. The identity of the person who stole and used the telephone password could not be ascertained. The plaintiff then filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting the defendant to compensate for the loss of telephone charges. The defendant argued that it had not stolen or used the plaintiff's telephone password to make international long-distance calls and that the compensation should be paid by the actual perpetrator, to be identified after the public security authorities complete their investigation. The defendant claimed it should not bear compensation liability until the situation was clarified.

The Dongshan District People's Court held that the telephone set of the defendant, Huanghua Printing House, was always under its actual possession and control. The use of the plaintiff, Jingxiutang Company's, telephone password to make international long-distance calls from that telephone caused economic losses to the plaintiff. The occurrence of the damage resulted from the defendant's failure to properly manage its telephone, and the defendant should bear liability. If a third party caused the damage using the telephone set under the defendant's actual control, the defendant should first compensate the plaintiff for the loss and then seek recourse from the third party. Accordingly, on June 25, 1991, the court rendered the following judgment: Within seven days from the effective date of this judgment, the defendant, Huanghua Printing House, shall pay the plaintiff, Jingxiutang Company, RMB 3,650.10 in telephone charges.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the defendant, Huanghua Printing House, appealed to the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court, reiterating the same defense arguments.

Upon trial, the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court held that the cause of the damage in this case was the appellant, Huanghua Printing House's, failure to properly manage its telephone. The appellant, Huanghua Printing House, should bear full compensation liability for the economic losses caused to the appellee, Jingxiutang Company, due to its own fault. The appellant's grounds for appeal were untenable. The first-instance judgment was correct and should be affirmed. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on April 6, 1994, the court rendered the following judgment: The appeal of the appellant, Huanghua Printing House, is dismissed, and the first-instance judgment is affirmed.
